title: Strip command quoting with default POSIX shlex splitting

note.title: Strip command quoting with default POSIX shlex splitting
answers: Why does Click use POSIX shlex splitting for pager and editor commands?
My quoted Windows pager path is not recognized.
How should an editor path containing spaces and flags be parsed?
note.body:
Symptom: A quoted pager executable path can retain its quote characters instead of becoming an unquoted executable token.
Root cause: src/click/_termui_impl.py:pager used shlex.split(..., posix=False), which retains quotes in tokens.
Fix pattern: Use default POSIX shlex.split for configured pager and editor commands; src/click/_termui_impl.py:Editor.edit_files follows the same parsing convention.
Constraints: Paths containing spaces require quoting or supported POSIX escaping. Covered examples include quoted Windows paths with flags and escaped spaces in Unix paths; tests/test_termui.py:test_editor_windows_path_normalization mocks Popen and checks unquoted argv, rather than establishing compatibility with every Windows command syntax.
note.applies: Parsing PAGER and configured editor command strings into subprocess arguments.
